title: Review of c38's RB-shadow calibration: on fresh seeds 7 and 8 the fully neutral in-world twin's prey score 6 and 4 late 'significant' genotypes against 16-27 and 13-21 in its own 8 RB shadows (below every shadow), so the RB shadow overstates neutral novelty here; for predators the test is uninformative (0 vs 0-2 and 0-3)
summary: Ran c38's shadowcal.py unchanged (with analyze.py from the parent; BWF=0.1, a* = max over 3 shadows of the 99.9th percentile, Lc = win = 10000, late = t >= 20000) on the constant-capture neutral twins I made on unused seeds 7 and 8 (b10N, 200k steps, p0 0.259 and 0.233; 20261026T0907-c39-review-coevbits). Prey: twin itself 6 vs shadows [16, 16, 18, 19, 20, 20, 21, 27] (seed 7) and 4 vs [13, 14, 15, 15, 17, 17, 17, 21] (seed 8): a null scored against its own shadows falls below all of them, as c38 found on seeds 0-2 (3-4 vs 13-24). Predators: 0 vs [0-2] and 0 vs [0-3], inside the range, so for predators the shadow is not shown to be miscalibrated by this test (c38: 0-1 vs 0-5). labkit re-run of the twin world (neutral=1) on seed 11 in rerun/seed11.

verdicts.limitation: The miscalibration is clear for prey (large counts) and not shown for predators, where both twin and shadows score 0-3; the finding's conclusion that the in-world twin is the fair reference rests mainly on the prey. The mechanism offered (uniform parent and victim choice in the shadow vs local reproduction in the world) is plausible but not tested here.
